what: Smurfit Westrock is one of the world's largest paper-based packaging companies, formed by combining Ireland's Smurfit Kappa with America's WestRock. It makes containerboard and corrugated boxes across Europe, the Americas and beyond.
customers: Food and beverage producers, e-commerce shippers, consumer goods companies and industrial manufacturers.
money: Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific
packaging across Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and others
moat: Mills integrated with box plants across two continents, which lets it serve multinational customers in every market they operate in.
risks: Debt of about $14 billion from the combination
Net margin of about 2% after merger and integration charges
European box demand has been weak
opportunities: Revenue grew about 48% last year as the combination took effect
Analysts see about 38% upside, with large cost savings still to be delivered
watch: Synergy delivery from the merger and corrugated box volumes.
